correctness.rationale: Every induced tree of K_{a,b} with an edge is a star, since two vertices in each shore induce a 4-cycle; all degrees odd forces odd positive leaf count. The labelled component EGF correctly subtracts the doubly oriented K_2. Every tree component uses odd positive numbers of vertices from both shores, enforcing component parity and c<=min(a,b); an explicit star-factor construction realizes every permitted c, including boundaries a=1 and a=2. The min-edge coefficient follows from surjections with odd fibers. Exhaustive direct edge-subset checks on 19 graphs (190798 subsets), and component-support checks on 180 pairs, agreed. These finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The primary literature explicitly poses optimization of maximum-edge 0-perfect forests and proves NP-hardness for arbitrary graphs. For the complete bipartite family this theorem solves the whole labelled component/edge polynomial rather than a scalar invariant, proves a precise parity-gapped attainable edge spectrum, gives minimum- and maximum-edge numbers, and counts extremal configurations. It identifies a structured, provably tractable case of a difficult and natural odd-degree induced-forest problem. The result is not claimed to generalize to arbitrary graphs.
